correctness.rationale: The p-adic identity is exact; for each p>m the unique original spike propagates on odd Pascal positions. For p<=m no two original valuations exceed floor(log_p m), and the proven high-spike lemma makes the residual exponent invariant under truncation at H. CRT yields the period, Lucas parity the exact degree, and residue equidistribution the finite atomic limit. Exact verifier checked 1,980 direct cells and 337 high-spike configurations. Finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The 2014 origin and 2015 closest full-text follow-up were inspected by their theorem statements and governing objects. Earlier results address prime-seeded Pascal support, the natural-seeded 2-adic slice, and eventual dynamics for an alternate squarefree-seeded triangle, not the asserted polynomial-times-periodic structure at every fixed natural-seed row for all primes. Exact record searches revealed no statement implying it; unindexed future/past literature remains a concrete risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently described fixed-row Z-game results could predate this work.
The explicit Q_m is grossly nonminimal, so the exact least-period question is not settled.
Related general finite-depth valuation stabilization methods might be published under another nomenclature.

value.rationale: This supplies an infinite structural classification for every fixed horizontal generation of a canonical number-theoretic growth game studied in archival papers, including a previously unrecognized polynomial degree controlled by binary digit sum, effective arithmetic periodic factors, and a limiting distribution. This is not a routine finite table extension or arbitrary invariant; it directly bridges Pascal-prime support with interacting small-prime effects.
